t: You're at the London Society of East Anglians War Memorial, in Liverpool Street station. Among the commuters, it stands as a place to remember the fallen. It was made by Guy Dawber, an architect who lived from 1861 to 1938. Dawber worked in the late Arts and Crafts style, and his work is particularly associated with the Cotswolds, so this is a piece by an architect best known for country buildings.
